origin.description: Guess the character set and language of each byte string with ICU.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, a raw vector, or a list of raw vectors.

arguments.name: filter_angle_brackets
arguments.text: If TRUE, drop text inside angle brackets before guessing.

origin.details: Guesses are ordered by decreasing confidence. An empty language is "". Failure is one missing row. A character string is read as its declared bytes.
origin.value: A list of data frames with columns Encoding, Language, and Confidence.
origin.example:
eng <- paste(rep("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.", 8), collapse = " ")
guess <- stri_enc_detect(eng)[[1]]$Encoding[[1]]
cat(paste0("stri_enc_detect on the English pangram repeated eight times guesses ", guess, " first.\n"))

translation.description: Guess the character set and language of each byte string with ICU.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, bytes, a list of strings, or a list of byte vectors. None is one missing value for a raw checker and an empty character vector for text.

arguments.name: filter_angle_brackets
arguments.text: If true, drop text inside angle brackets before guessing.

translation.details: Guesses are ordered by decreasing confidence. An empty language is "". Failure is one missing row. A Python string is read as UTF-8 bytes. A bytes object is one raw vector.
translation.value: A dict with Encoding, Language, and Confidence, or a list of those dicts. Confidence uses NA on failure.
translation.example:
from stringi.encoding import stri_enc_detect
eng = " ".join(["The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."] * 8)
guess = stri_enc_detect(eng)["Encoding"][0]
print(f"stri_enc_detect on the English pangram repeated eight times guesses {guess} first.")
